title: Hungarian Greek Catholic revised Liturgikon and Chrysostom replacement extract, with scoped approval and reception

traditions.label: Hungarian Greek Catholic Hajdúdorog received service books
traditions.scope: The 1920 revised combined Liturgikon and its 1949 Chrysostom extract, in Hungarian with Greek canonical parts in the full book.
traditions.coverage_note: The books have explicit local private-use publishing permission and separately evidenced operative reception. The dossier does not equate private permission with general public-language authorization or establish a seventeenth-century-to-present chain.

sources.title: István Ivancsó, Miklósy István hajdúdorogi megyéspüspök liturgikus rendelkezései, Athanasiana 26 (2007), pp. 65–87
sources.inspection: Acquired full issue; printed pp. 65–73 read, p. 69 visually inspected. Reports the 1920 book and quotes directive 1021/1921 on using its revised text. At pp. 72–73 quotes distribution circular 1195/1921 and transcribes private-use permission 1235/1920. Full original book and circulars were not inspected.
sources.limitations: Primary documents quoted through scholarship. Private-use printing permission, a local directive and reported actual reception have distinct scopes; no Holy See public-language approval or uniform parish compliance is established. Earlier 1793 Krucsay attribution in this source is not used.

sources.title: István Ivancsó, A magyar Liturgikon a hajdúdorogi egyházmegyében, Athanasiana 27 (2008), pp. 11–28
sources.inspection: Acquired full issue; printed pp. 19–25 read, pp. 20–21 and 24 visually inspected. Quotes the 1920 book’s Emlékezetül pp. 309–310, records 22 August 1920 printing permission, reports 1921 release and quotes Dudás’s 2351/1949 circular describing the worn 1920 Chrysostom section and two formats of replacement extract. The 1984 reprint is expressly unchanged.
sources.limitations: Original books and circulars not acquired. Its table gives 1235/1920 for the 1949 title, against 1650/1949 reported by Ivancsó 2003. Neither number is silently preferred. The books’ whole contents and modern reception after this source’s date are not independently collated.

sources.title: 1920-imprint Liturgikon title leaf photographed in AbeBooks item 32188629463 (Time-Honored Books)
sources.inspection: All four offered photographs acquired and visually inspected. Photograph 4 shows the unnumbered title leaf with 1235/1920 private-use permission, revised/expanded statement, Hajdúdorog episcopal office and Jóba Elek printer line 1723–1920. Photographs 1–3 show binding and endpapers only.
sources.limitations: Four offered seller photographs acquired and inspected: front cover, spine/cover, endpapers, and an unnumbered title leaf. Only the fourth photograph carries printed book text. It verifies the reproduced title, 1235/1920 private-use permission, revised/expanded editorial statement and Jóba Elek printer line 1723–1920. No permission-date verso, contents, Greek anaphora pages, terminal leaves or Emlékezetül pp. 309–310 are shown. The seller calls the book a 1920 first edition, but the physical impression cannot be independently authenticated from these four photographs: the known 1984 facsimile retains the 1920 imprint. No full 1920 book or complete textual state is acquired. A binding appearance cannot establish a print date.

sources.title: Szent Atanáz college library catalogue, bibNY56K501 / recnum 448: revised and expanded Liturgikon (1920)
sources.inspection: Complete MARC and long-with-holdings records read. MARC 001 identifies bibNY56K501; 250 gives revised/expanded; 260 gives Jóba Elek, Nyíregyháza, 1920; 300 gives 311 pages, illustrations, 24 cm. Holdings are Ant10911/M-1638, Ant10792/M-1637 and Ant101011/M-1891. The M-1637 copy lacks pp. 273–311; its catalogued front annotations include Melles's 16 August 1920 presentation and Szemerszky's August 1920 note about preparation and Greek-text correction. Ant101011/M-1891 bears Hajdúböszörmény Greek Catholic parish stamps. M-1638 was re-bound in 2019.
sources.limitations: Full catalogue records read, original physical copies and annotations not inspected. The catalogue lists three separate copies, including an incomplete annotated copy; they must not be merged with the seller copy. No digital object or MARC 856 field is present in the returned record. Parish stamps and ownership annotations do not by themselves date liturgical use. Catalogue transcription is an acquisition route, not a replacement for original-book collation.

sources.title: Szent Atanáz college library catalogue, bibNY56K11755 / recnum 10613: Aranyszájú Szent János liturgy (1949)
sources.inspection: Complete MARC and long-with-holdings records read. MARC 246 transcribes private-use permission 1650/1949; 260 names Orosz Károly, Nyíregyháza, 1949; 300 gives 59 pages plus 5 typed pages. Holdings are D 442, DT 399, DT 484 and C 12647. Copy DT 484 has typed additions numbered 60–80; copy 104641/C 12647 has five typed pages with prayers for the sick, petitions and Communion prayers. These are explicitly copy-specific additions.
sources.limitations: Full catalogue records read; no original title image or full 1949 book acquired. MARC 246 transcribes 1650/1949 private-use permission and corroborates Ivancsó 2003, but does not independently resolve its disagreement with Ivancsó 2008's 1235/1920. Copy-specific typed supplements are not part of the printed 59-page extent and do not establish another printed recension. No digital object or MARC 856 field is present in the returned record.

stages.label: Hajdúdorog revised and expanded Liturgikon
stages.date_label: Attested off press and awaiting distribution in early 1921; bears 1920 imprint and printing permission of 22 August 1920
stages.scope: The combined Hungarian service book, with the canonical parts also in Greek, incorporating Chrysostom, Basil and Presanctified with the offices and calendar. Local private-use approval and operative reception are separately qualified.
stages.witness_label: Nyíregyháza, Jóba Elek, 1920-imprint title photographed in a seller copy whose impression is unconfirmed; 311 pages per college catalogue, complete book unacquired
stages.summary: The revised and expanded book bearing a 1920 imprint is attested off press and awaiting distribution in early 1921. It combines the earlier separately issued liturgies and adds Greek canonical parts, offices, calendar and paschalion. The 1921 wording directive documents operative local reception, with private-use permission explicit.

evidence.locus: Printed pp. 19–21, especially p. 20 and notes 31–34; p. 24 title table
evidence.claim: Identifies the book, the 1235/1920 private-use printing permission, preparation/release sequence and expanded components. The early-1921 announcement attests the book already off press and awaiting distribution, rather than proving exact publication in either 1920 or 1921.

evidence.locus: Printed pp. 69–73; circular 1021/1921 quoted at pp. 69–71
evidence.claim: Documents direction to use the revised wording and describes the book as operative in the eparchy; this is distinct from the earlier printing permission.
Dudás describes the heavily worn Chrysostom sections of copies in use, corroborating actual reception of the 1920 book before 1949.

The photographed leaf reproduces the 1920 imprint, 1235/1920 private-use permission and revised/expanded editorial statement. It does not show the 22 August permission date or authenticate the physical impression against the later facsimile.
Identifies three exact college copies, 311-page catalogue extent and the incomplete annotated M-1637 copy. Original annotations and terminal pagination are not inspected.

stages.limitations: No exact complete book or original approval/circular scan acquired. The stage uses the early-1921 attestation of a book already off press and awaiting distribution. Its 1920 imprint, summer preparation and 22 August 1920 printing permission do not establish an exact publication date; neither does the early-1921 announcement exclude late-1920 printing. First celebration remains unknown. The printed permission is for private use, and no general Holy See authorization or present obligation follows. Scholarly descriptions do not authorize text inheritance. Batch 3 adds only a photographed title and exact catalogue-copy routes. The title image does not authenticate the seller's physical impression, which may require comparison with the known facsimile. The permission date, contents, Greek canonical sections and terminal Emlékezetül remain uninspected.
stages.reception: Local operational wording is documented by the 1921 directive; worn copies are described in the 1949 episcopal circular through scholarship. Geographic extent, first use, individual parish compliance and later modifications remain unproved.

stages.label: Hajdúdorog Chrysostom replacement extract
stages.date_label: 1949 publication and episcopal announcement; permission number discrepant in the literature
stages.scope: The Chrysostom section of the 1920 service book reissued as an extract, in a bind-in replacement format and a separately titled format; not another complete liturgikon recension.
stages.witness_label: Aranyszájú Szent János egyházatya szent és isteni liturgiája, Nyíregyháza, Orosz Károly, 1949; reported 59 pages
stages.summary: Dudás commissioned a replacement for worn Chrysostom sections. One format could be bound into the older 1920 book, the other separately; variable intention formularies were omitted. A changed format and reduced extent do not establish a newly revised anaphora.

evidence.locus: Printed pp. 21–22 and 24; 2351/1949 circular quoted at p. 21
evidence.claim: Identifies the 1949 extract, its practical replacement purpose, two physical formats and omission of variable intention formularies.
Describes the 1949 publication as an unchanged-text extract of the 1920 book.

The holding catalogue transcribes private-use permission 1650/1949, supplies exact copy routes and distinguishes typed additions from 59 printed pages. This corroborates one secondary reading but does not replace original-title inspection.

stages.limitations: Full original copy and the 1949 circular were not inspected. Ivancsó 2003 gives private-use permission 1650/1949; Ivancsó 2008 gives 1235/1920. Approval number remains unresolved; no substantive new textual recension or first date of actual use is claimed. Holding-library catalogue bibNY56K11755 corroborates 1650/1949; original-title inspection is still needed before resolving the disagreement. Typed additions in particular copies do not establish new printed textual states.
stages.reception: Episcopal commissioning and distribution are reported by the quoted 1949 circular. Its replacement purpose concerns the operative 1920 book; no independent altar-use event of a named surviving 1949 copy was found.

transitions.summary: A practical extract reissues the Chrysostom component for replacement or independent binding. This is witness and component succession, with no demonstrated new recension.

evidence.claim: The bishop’s announcement relates the 1949 extract directly to worn Chrysostom sections of the 1920 book.
The 1949 witness is described as an unchanged-text extract.

transitions.limitations: No independent whole-text collation. This edge records a described extract relationship and does not grant literal inheritance or exact-copy identity.

gaps.missing: Dated Nyírderzs use, the unidentified Kriva/Krive church in the 1666 note, and a supported sequence of exact Slavonic service books. Habina’s ownership and a separate museum colophon do not establish such a chain. Batch 4 (2026-10-21): The college OPAC adds undated provenance for both 1646 copies (a possessor entry naming Fr. István Zolcsák, Nyírderzs, which may record only the 2010 transfer; a Nyírpazony parish-office stamp, catalogue locus 74. táblaoldal); a catalogue-transcribed memorial note, written after 1881, recording that a Przemyśl 1840 Sluzhebnik was offered in 1856 for the use of the Sátoraljaújhely Greek Catholic church; and two undated copies, a Mikóháza copy of that edition with inserted Hungarian translations and a Lviv 1780 copy of catalogue-bracketed Abaújszántó provenance with references to Hungarian page numbers. These locate Slavonic books in Greek Catholic parishes now in Hungary; none is an inspected original, an approval or a dated first use.
gaps.next_source: M–920 (Ant 10467) ownership leaves 102–109 and dated Nyírderzs parish inventories; Eger Uu.III.8 original terminal colophon; Földvári–Ojtozi 1992 catalogue item 4 and the original 1775 estate list. Batch 3 identifies the separate Google copy as Czech Slovanská knihovna A 003340 (SLK000577538); its own front/title and terminal leaves are missing. It cannot supply the missing original M–920 ownership leaves or substitute for dated Nyírderzs use. Batch 4 (2026-10-21): Inspect Szent Atanáz copies Ant30125 (memorial note recording the 1856 donation), Ant30146 (Hungarian insertions) and Ant30101 (Hungarian page references) and identify the Hungarian book cited; these copy leads are deferred origin-review inventory records hungarian-satoraljaujhely-przemysl1840-copies and hungarian-abaujszanto-lviv1780-copies. Batch 5 (2026-10-22): a further defective public copy catalogued as the Lviv 1646 edition (Ukrainian Catholic University digital library item 156, Mshanets provenance, leaves 14-297 and two unnumbered; canvases 3, 563, 566, 568 and 570 viewed) has no title, colophon or Hungarian provenance and is less complete than the Czech copy A 003340 above; it adds no title, colophon or reception evidence. No dated Nyírderzs evidence was found.
gaps.consequence: No reception edge connects Lviv 1646 or the Vilnius/Supraśl edition to the Hungarian 1920 book.

gaps.missing: Exact original service books, original circulars and resolution of the 1949 permission number. The distinction between private-use printing permission, normative local wording and public-language authorization remains explicit.
gaps.next_source: Acquire the 1920 book including its permission and Emlékezetül pp. 309–310, both 1949 formats including title/permission leaves, circulars 1021/1921, 1195/1921 and 2351/1949, and Ivancsó Dokumentáció I (2006), pp. 44–54. Batch 3 acquisition routes: college OPAC bibNY56K501/recnum448 has Ant10911/M-1638, Ant10792/M-1637 (pp.273–311 missing) and Ant101011/M-1891; bibNY56K11755/recnum10613 has D442, DT399, DT484 and C12647. Original copy-specific annotations and typed supplements remain uninspected. Current official GMFL finding aid (https://hd.gorogkatolikus.hu/leveltar/fond_es_allagjegyzek.pdf, 2025-, p.1) lists circulars I–1–h, 4.886 linear metres; Arca https://arca.melte.hu/index.php/korlevelek-12 gives HU GMFL I.01.h. Exact original1021/1921,1195/1921 and2351/1949 issues remain needed. Separate Nyíregyháza parish box28 (circulars1903–1989) and Penészlek box15 (1913–1967) are series-level routes; exact issue completeness is unverified. Batch 5 (2026-10-22): not attempted; no new route to the 1920 or 1949 originals or the Hajdúdorog circulars was tried (the Google Books HTTP 429 recorded this batch concerned the Czech 1646 copy, not these books).
gaps.consequence: Documentary book states and the described extract relationship are available; exact liturgical text, legal scope beyond the printed permission and substantive prayer changes remain uncollated.

gaps.missing: Original 1954 rubric directives, later operative revisions and exact editions currently used. The reported unchanged 1984 printing does not establish a new textual state. Batch 4 (2026-10-21): The college OPAC lists a Hungarian–Romani (Cerhari) Chrysostom liturgy with the cataloguer-supplied imprint [Nyíregyháza]: [Hajdúdorogi Egyházmegye], [2012] (91 p., translator Péter Lakatos); this is a deferred translation lead, not an operative Hungarian Liturgikon state, and no Greek Catholic Hungarian Liturgikon edition later than 1949 appears among the 106 subject-liturgikon records read (a bounded catalogue result, not proof that none exists).
gaps.next_source: Dudás directive 819 in circular 1954/XIII; exact 1984 reprint and its 1983/1984 correspondence; later local rubric/translation decrees and dated named-copy use. Batch 3 also leaves original819/1954 open. Current GMFL I–1–h and the separately described parish circular collections are acquisition targets, with no scanned original directive or named-copy altar-use event acquired.
gaps.consequence: No continuous or present-day adoption claim is inferred from the two documented states.
